steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The US film industry is dominated by the major Hollywood studios — Warner Bros, Disney, Universal, Paramount, Columbia and Fox — which control the majority of film production and distribution worldwide.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Production involves the development, financing and creation of a film, including pre-production planning, principal photography and post-production editing, effects and sound design.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Distribution is the process of marketing and delivering films to audiences through theatrical releases, home entertainment and digital platforms, with studios investing heavily in promotional campaigns.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Exhibition refers to the screening of films to audiences, historically dominated by cinema chains but now including streaming platforms that have transformed how audiences access film content.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use specific studio examples — Disney, Warner Bros, Universal — rather than discussing 'Hollywood' vaguely. Understand the distinction between production, distribution and exhibition and explain how they interact within the industry. Link industry practices to audience experience: how do distribution strategies affect what audiences watch and how? Use contemporary examples to show understanding of how the industry is changing — streaming, franchise filmmaking, global markets. Explain how conglomeration and vertical integration shape the films that get made, not just how they structure the business.
